answer: Each identity also needs a unique sponsor from an established grove of trusted peers, making fake accounts costly to seed. New agents must stake tokens that vest slowly, like a glacier grinding forward, releasing reputation only after several epochs of verified work. A lightweight zephyr of random peer challenges then samples behavior, and any agent failing twice forfeits its stake. Attackers must burn real capital across many sponsors and survive sustained audits, so mass sybil creation becomes economically irrational. In practice, Agent0020 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
